step: Settle the U.S. side before you move anything.
detail: Reconstruct foreign-account balances year by year and have a U.S. adviser assess FBAR, Form 8938 and any Form 3520 exposure. The FBAR maximum is $16,536 non-willful and $165,353 willful per violation; moving the money first does not reduce it.

step: Assemble the source-of-funds file.
detail: Employment contract or service agreement, payroll or invoice records, and the tax evidence — a tax payment certificate, an exemption certificate or the filing form. Art. 59 requires documents showing the transaction amount and including tax certificates.

step: Ask the branch in writing which article it will apply.
detail: Art. 59 for a 境外个人, or arts. 54-57 if the bank classified you as a 境内个人. The two definitions of 境内个人 differ and the bank's classification is not visible from outside.

step: Buy the dollars at the counter or in mobile banking.
detail: You pay the bank's selling rate. On the 2026-11-11 10:25:02 board that is 6.6911 against a buying rate of 6.6630, so 0.20998% of every dollar is the rate cost.

step: Instruct one wire for the whole amount.
detail: The fee is 1 per mille with a RMB 50 floor and a RMB 260 ceiling, plus a RMB 150 telegraph charge. Above about $38,857 the fee is pinned at the ceiling, so one wire is always cheapest.

step: Choose the charge option deliberately.
detail: 'OUR' makes you pay the intermediary charges up front and is the only way to learn what they actually are. Intermediary and receiving-bank charges are not published anywhere and are left blank on this site.

step: Reconcile the received amount against the sent amount.
detail: The difference is your true intermediary cost. Record it; it is the one number on this page that no official source can give you.

step: Confirm what is actually in the FX account.
detail: Ask the branch for a statement of every account in your name and its currency. Dollars already there need no conversion.

step: Wire it out on your passport.
detail: No purchase, so no spread. The wire fee is the same 1 per mille / RMB 50-260 plus RMB 150 telegraph.

step: Do not top the FX account up from RMB first.
detail: That would be a conversion and would attract the 0.20998% spread. Only the dollars genuinely already there avoid it.

step: Confirm you actually hold the 外国人永久居留身份证.
detail: Without the card this route does not exist for you; the annual convenience amount is expressly limited to card holders.

step: Plan one calendar year per USD 50,000.
detail: Above the annual amount you either need source documents (which makes this M01) or you buy year by year. Eight wires on $400,000 costs $1,330.12 against $901.20 for one.

step: Never use anyone else's amount.
detail: Splitting a quota across people is treated as evasion under Decree 532 art. 39 and puts the people involved on a watch list for the year and the next two.

step: Cancel the Chinese household registration and settle tax first.
detail: The IIT law requires tax to be cleared BEFORE the hukou is cancelled. Get the cancellation certificate from the public security office.

step: Apply to the SAFE branch at your former hukou location.
detail: Written application, applicant form, ID, cancellation certificate, settlement-abroad proof certified by a Chinese embassy or consulate, property-right documents, and the tax payment certificate.

step: Note what 2014 removed.
detail: No RMB 500,000 head-office filing. No staged remittance — the bank may remit once or in instalments inside the approved amount. No notarisation of property documents or of the agency agreement.

step: Instruct the bank with the approval in hand.
detail: The bank must remit straight to your own account abroad; cash withdrawal in China is not permitted. Bank cost is the same 0.20998% spread plus the wire fee.

step: Gather the inheritance evidence.
detail: Proof of inheritance, the decedent's property-right documents, and a tax payment certificate from the tax authority where the property sits. Notarisation is no longer required.

step: Apply to the SAFE branch at the decedent's last hukou location.
detail: Since 2014 several inheritances can be combined at one decedent's hukou location instead of applying separately.

step: Remit to your own account abroad.
detail: Directly to the beneficiary's account in the country of residence. No cash in China.

step: Price the whole two-leg route before you start.
detail: The first leg saves about $10.46 per wire on the telegraph charge (RMB 80 not RMB 150). The onward leg from Hong Kong to the U.S. is unpriced here and could easily cost more than that.

step: Treat this as a corporate question, not a personal one.
detail: Corporate income tax first, then a 20% dividend, then the remittance on a board resolution and the tax filing form. Nothing on this site prices the corporate leg.
